It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

A client-only public catalog reader and tool-access preview can use bounded anonymous GETs and project no credentials or account facts. Defensive response/time/concurrency bounds are implementation limits, not claimed production capacity or service SLA. Desktop bootstrap recognition is only a contract check, never authorization.

RU-011 should replace the candidate's CLI-first landing experience with a desktop-application-first native-feeling shell, a distinct vegetable-leaf brand icon, a bounded two-application local discovery projection, and a beginner flow from application choice through line and real model selection to an honestly blocked connection step. CLI discovery remains secondary, and server login, secrets, configuration writes, installation, updating, payment and production resources remain outside the unit.

RU-023 should supersede RU-022 as an internal desktop 0.2.0 integration candidate: validate the fixed NewAPI v2 bootstrap on either compiled first-party line, complete system-browser device authorization, retain refresh credentials only in the operating-system credential store, keep access credentials in native memory, return only sanitized account, cumulative usage, model and comparable price projections to the renderer, and open only the bootstrap-provided first-party wallet URL. Tool-key creation, configuration writes, telemetry, updater and server changes remain excluded, and production release remains blocked until the v2 branch is deployed with server-enforced desktop-session route restrictions.

RU-024 should supersede RU-023 as an internal functional client candidate: make the first-party desktop session line-independent, project NewAPI status USD/CNY settings, share account state across the shell, use the authenticated model list, and add one native-only setup command for Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex. The command reuses or creates one dedicated unrestricted tool token per target, validates the selected account model and compiled origin, writes only owned fields with transaction-scoped in-memory rollback, returns no credential or path, and retains no backup history. DSH, other tools, server code, deployment, updater, telemetry and public release remain outside the unit.

A bounded successor should treat publication as an explicit operator action rather than a legal-document validator: publish only exact bytes synchronized from compiled official origins, preserve immutable hash-bound objects, distinguish operator-native preverification from client-native-required artifacts, and require the client to perform its unchanged native trust check in both cases. An atomic empty catalog is the remote kill switch and every unusable mirror state falls back to the official source without credentials or a client update.

Replace seven adapter-specific blocking verification definitions with one activation state machine: validate eligibility, obtain native credentials, atomically commit and read back owned settings, start only helper-owned local runtimes, and handle desktop reload through explicit normal-quit consent. Observe the first real user request asynchronously instead of gating configuration on it.

Complete one bounded Yeschoy self-update closure: a native-only signed updater with background check and explicit one-click download/restart UX, cooperative shutdown and recovery, immutable artifact plus atomic manifest publication, a truthful unavailable state, and a Yeschoy-specific release workflow. Isolate its state, mutex, IPC contract, origin channel and signing authority from tool activation, third-party application downloads, account/model services and renderer updater permissions.

Create one bounded public-release remediation unit that closes repository-owned security, resource-control, recovery, installer, update-publication, platform-exit and UX truth gaps without packaging or remote mutation. Make release automation fail closed when signing, notarization or publication credentials are absent, and retain those external credentials plus live promotion as explicit release gates rather than claiming completion.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
V1 serves novice users who already installed their AI tools but do not know how to configure them; tool installation is deferred.
V1 supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH (DeepSeek Harness).
The official mainland-optimized line root is https://yeschoy.com and the Cloudflare global-acceleration line root is https://api.yeschoy.com.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

V1 keeps no persistent configuration-backup history. Before a material configuration write it creates only an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot; successful validation deletes it immediately, failure restores from it and deletes it after recovery, and a crash leaves only an unfinished-transaction snapshot for recovery on the next launch.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

The product owner confirmed the Claude Code and Codex credential-helper rule: their per-tool relay keys stay in the operating-system credential vault, unsupported versions must prompt for upgrade, and the client must never fall back to plaintext key storage for compatibility.

The product owner confirmed that DSH V1 formally supports one-click configuration only for the web profile; headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp, and other profiles are read-only discovery targets and must not be modified in V1.

The product owner confirmed the V1 secure credential integration for the remaining tools: OpenCode uses a signed authentication plugin whose runtime loader calls the credential helper, Pi uses its native command-backed apiKey contract, and DSH uses a version-pinned operating-system-vault credential provider. Missing or incompatible security components must block configuration with no plaintext fallback.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner rejected presenting DSH as a Developer Preview and stated that the current DSH version is materially settled. DSH web is therefore a normal V1 support target after exact-version verification, without a product preview badge; this product decision does not convert the upstream prerelease tag into an official stable release or prove compatibility before testing.

The product owner confirmed that incomplete DSH web compatibility must not block the overall V1 release. If no exact DSH version has passed the mandatory matrix at release time, DSH remains discovery-only with no configuration or credential writes until a later trusted client update adds verified support.

The product owner authorized development to begin with a governed first release unit limited to the 野菜API desktop shell, product branding, and read-only discovery and compatibility reporting for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH; account login, billing, recharge, NewAPI changes, secrets, configuration writes, automatic updates, and telemetry are excluded from this unit.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

The product owner authorized one continuous goal to finish the client-side 野菜API V1 candidate without incremental approval pauses, while preserving the existing prohibition on changing NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production and without fabricating backend-dependent success.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: What bounded implementation unit may finish the client-side V1 candidate after RU-004 without implying that backend-dependent or release-security capabilities are ready?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-005 as a client-side V1 candidate successor that supersedes RU-004. Preserve the account, billing, five-tool discovery, and configuration-preview truth boundaries; add one beginner home journey, a user-triggered read-only diagnostic that resolves and attempts TCP port 443 only for yeschoy.com and api.yeschoy.com without credentials or API payloads, and a settings and security surface that exposes language, privacy, secret, backup, update, and release state. Prepare but do not publish Windows and macOS candidate bundles, keep updater artifacts and telemetry upload disabled, label Windows unsigned beta limitations and macOS signing and notarization as unmet release gates, and update the future NewAPI handoff without modifying any server or production resource.

decisions.question: How should the audited public-release defects be repaired without repeating local fixes, hiding external release blockers or coupling all integrations to one application-specific path?
decisions.choice: Implement a single dependency-closed remediation unit across the shared native bridge, account, activation, discovery, installation, update and workbench boundaries. Authenticate before buffering, apply one shared admission guard to large local requests, create model-scoped dedicated keys, expose bounded activation progress and cooperative cancellation, make logout recovery explicit, bound child-process output, validate Windows identities and use qualified launchers, and make installer and language claims match verified coverage. Remove inherited CC Switch publication assumptions, verify updater signatures before promotion, and make signing, notarization and live stable-channel publication fail-closed release gates. Do not package, upload, deploy, bump a version or claim public readiness in this unit.

decisions.question: How should the repaired public-release tree be governed after RU-074 was correctly rejected for touching three paths outside its frozen ownership?

Create RU-075 as a source-readonly verification successor with no work-package dependency on the failed implementation run; execute the same six exact semantic scenarios against the final current tree under mandatory source isolation. Do not change product behavior, tests, packages, servers, DNS, credentials, signing state or release claims after dispatch. Packaging, native signatures, notarization, live promotion and clean-system smoke tests remain external unpassed gates.

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: V1 detects installed instances of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports installed, not found, configured, needs attention, and unsupported-version states.
acceptance: Every supported tool has an explicit detection contract and version evidence.
Not found is not presented as an error.
An unsupported or ambiguous installation is not modified.

requirements.statement: The guided configuration flow selects a line and model, previews the change, creates an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot, writes only owned fields, validates the result, tests connectivity, and rolls back on failure without retaining backup history.
acceptance: Unrelated user configuration survives a successful change.
A failed write or validation restores the exact pre-operation state.
Concurrent external edits produce a visible conflict instead of a silent overwrite.

requirements.statement: The client exposes a mainland-optimized line rooted at https://yeschoy.com and a Cloudflare global-acceleration line rooted at https://api.yeschoy.com, with the effective tool endpoint visible in advanced details.
acceptance: The labels and root endpoints match the accepted line decision.
Protocol-specific path rules are applied by each tool adapter rather than stored as a misleading universal suffix.
The selected effective endpoint is inspectable before configuration.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: V1 does not download, install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
acceptance: A missing tool receives installation guidance only.
No V1 action elevates privileges to install a third-party tool.

requirements.statement: The current product phase remains client-only and produces a separate future NewAPI change specification without applying backend or production changes.
acceptance: No NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, or production configuration is modified in this phase.
Backend-dependent capabilities remain visibly specified or unavailable rather than simulated as complete.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: V1 automatically configures a third-party tool only when that exact tool version is present in the signed compatibility allowlist backed by complete platform, credential, configuration, request, conflict, recovery, removal, and secret-leak evidence.
acceptance: Every allowlisted version names its exact upstream tag or package version, adapter-contract version, supported platform cells, evidence set, and client catalog version.
A minimum-version comparison, an open semantic-version range, source-level feature presence, or a successful test on only one platform cannot independently grant automatic-configuration support.

A newly released, unknown, prerelease, failed, unparsable, or multiply installed version stays read-only and cannot create credentials, write configuration, install plugins, or alter defaults unless its exact identity is explicitly allowlisted.

Each allowlisted platform cell passes detection, configuration preview, credential delivery, atomic write and read-back, real tool-level request, override and conflict handling, interrupted-transaction recovery, receipt-matching removal, and complete-secret scanning.
Compatibility allowlist changes ship only inside a signed client or signed compatibility artifact governed by the updater trust boundary, and a stale or unverifiable catalog fails closed.

An exact DSH upstream prerelease tag may be allowlisted only after the full matrix passes; when it passes, it is presented as normal V1 support without a product preview badge while its exact upstream version remains visible, and it does not imply support for another DSH tag or profile.

requirements.statement: Incomplete DSH web compatibility does not block the overall V1 release; until an exact DSH version completes every mandatory gate, DSH remains discovery-only with no configuration or credential writes and may gain normal support only through a later trusted signed client update.
acceptance: The overall V1 release-readiness result is not failed solely because no exact DSH web version has yet completed every required platform and security cell.

An unverified DSH installation is visibly reported as detected but not currently supported for automatic configuration and exposes no configure, repair, remove, line-switch, model-write, plugin-install, or credential action.
Allowing the overall release never relaxes the exact-version allowlist, credential-vault, no-plaintext-fallback, web-profile-only, or truthful-support-display boundaries.
A later signed client update may add normal DSH support only after an exact version passes the complete matrix; discovery-only status does not silently convert into support.
Release notes, product pages, and in-app supported-tool lists state the actually verified tool set and do not claim DSH automatic configuration before evidence exists.

requirements.statement: RU-001 provides a beginner-readable 野菜API desktop shell that performs only local read-only discovery of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports exact detected versions and conservative compatibility truth without contacting a server or changing the machine.
acceptance: The primary screen names 野菜API and explains in plain language that it is checking already-installed tools without asking for an API key, Base URL, model name, or configuration-file path.

One explicit scan returns exactly one result for each of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and distinguishes not found, detected but unverified, executable failure or timeout, and ambiguous multiple-installation states.

Every detected version string remains visible; a version not present in a later verified exact-version allowlist is reported as read-only and exposes no configure, repair, remove, install, line, model, credential, login, billing, recharge, updater, or telemetry action.
The scan performs no HTTP or other network request, does not read tool configuration contents, does not access a credential store, and creates, modifies, or deletes no user or tool file.
A failed or timed-out probe affects only that tool card, keeps the other tool results visible, provides a safe rescan action, and never guesses installation or compatibility.
Repeated scans replace stale results by request identity so an older completion cannot overwrite the newest visible scan.

requirements.statement: RU-002 preserves RU-001 and adds a beginner-readable account and billing shell that truthfully reports the missing desktop backend boundary without contacting account services, storing credentials, fabricating values, or enabling recharge.
acceptance: The shell exposes clear Account and Local tools destinations and preserves the complete fixed five-tool read-only scan behavior from RU-001.
The account destination states that secure website authorization requires a future server upgrade and exposes no control that pretends authorization can currently begin or complete.
Balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge remain visibly unavailable instead of showing zero, sample, cached, or inferred values.
The fixed 1 USD = 6.75 CNY comparison rate is labelled display-only and not presented as a live exchange rate or a billing input.

The runtime makes no account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, or other network request and persists no password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, API key, account profile, or scan history.

The updated future NewAPI specification is pinned to current official GitHub evidence, distinguishes current routes from proposed /api/desktop/v1 routes, and records the deployed 404 readiness result without changing NewAPI or production infrastructure.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: RU-005 preserves all prior truthful client boundaries and completes a cohesive client-side V1 candidate with beginner guidance, bounded two-line connectivity evidence, settings and security truth, complete multilingual states, candidate bundle preparation, and an actionable future NewAPI handoff without claiming production or backend readiness.
acceptance: The default destination gives a beginner one ordered path through local tool discovery, line choice and preview, account integration truth, and diagnostics, with no API, Base URL, configuration-file, or secret knowledge required.

The account and billing destination still displays no fabricated login, balance, usage, model ID, official price, actual price, or recharge result, and configuration apply remains disabled for every tool and line.

Connectivity runs only after an explicit user action, checks exactly yeschoy.com:443 and api.yeschoy.com:443 through a closed local query, returns only bounded DNS and TCP outcomes with latency and correlation, sends no HTTP or model request, and never accesses or uploads a credential, cookie, prompt, response, configuration, complete local path, or raw network error.

The diagnostic UI distinguishes default, processing, partial success, complete failure, stale result, invalid projection, and recovery, and explicitly says TCP reachability does not prove API, account, model, or billing health.

Settings makes language selection, no-retained-backup policy, secret boundary, inactive telemetry upload, inactive updater, candidate version, and release gates visible without exposing an action that exceeds current authority.

A candidate-only Tauri bundle overlay exists for local Windows and macOS packaging while automatic updater artifacts remain disabled; the release checklist requires native-platform builds, macOS Developer ID signing and notarization for direct public distribution, and an explicit unsigned-Windows beta warning until a real signing path exists.
All four supported languages contain the candidate navigation and page copy, the UI remains usable at 320 CSS pixels, and keyboard focus remains visible.

The future NewAPI handoff names the exact interfaces needed for authorization, bootstrap, account, usage, models, server-projected official-versus-actual prices, tool keys, telemetry, compatibility catalog, and update separation while recording that none is deployed or modified by RU-005.

requirements.statement: RU-007 supplies a real anonymous first-party model/group catalog and protocol-aware five-tool preview plus an implementable backend handoff while server, credential, account and configuration-write authority remain absent.
acceptance: Only explicit user action can request the three fixed GET paths on one compiled HTTPS origin; no custom URLs, redirects, auth headers, cookies, raw upstream errors, expressions or persisted metadata reach the renderer.

Public catalog facts are labelled non-user-specific; groups are independent of network lines; models retain real IDs and declared protocols while installation compatibility, group-specific stream restrictions and account authorization remain unverified.
Line changes, refreshes and unmounts invalidate prior requests and selections; malformed, partial and failed responses never fall back to sample models, default ratios or cached authentication.

Claude Code requires declared anthropic, Codex requires openai-response, OpenCode and Pi require openai for this preview profile; DSH continues to abstain. Missing declarations block the corresponding preview without claiming that a positive declaration proves real compatibility.

No balance or actual account price is fabricated. Server display exchange rate and fixed 6.75 official comparison FX are distinct. No numeric price projection or client expression execution is introduced.

Bootstrap absence, transport failure, unsupported contract and recognized contract are distinguishable; recognition cannot activate login or apply. The backend handoff includes schema, examples, actual deployed-source evidence, missing services and server-owned acceptance.
Existing candidate regression plus new contract, protocol, race/recovery, UI and handoff tests pass; current native suite compiles and runs without skipped tests.

requirements.statement: RU-011 supersedes the candidate's command-line-first presentation with a branded desktop-application-first beginner experience for Claude Desktop and the Codex desktop surface while preserving truthful client-only, security and server boundaries.
acceptance: The installed application and every bundled installer use an original 野菜API icon rather than the inherited upstream icon, and the icon is declared in the base Tauri bundle configuration for macOS and Windows outputs.

The primary home destination detects exactly Claude Desktop and the Codex desktop surface through bounded local application locations and identifiers, never substitutes a claude or codex command for a desktop application, never returns a complete user path, and rejects stale or structurally incomplete projections.

The default navigation and application cards lead with desktop applications, recognizable app identities, installation state and the next beginner action; command-line discovery remains reachable only as a secondary advanced destination.

The setup destination presents desktop application, line and real public model ID as the visible path and hides Base URL, configuration file and credential implementation details from the primary flow.

Claude Desktop and Codex desktop configuration remain explicitly unverified and unapplied until their separate documented adapters, first-party account boundary, secure credentials and exact-version evidence exist; no detected application is described as connected or configured.

The visual system uses the frozen cool garden palette, clear Chinese-first typography, compact desktop navigation and application-tray signature; keyboard focus, reduced motion and a usable 320 CSS pixel layout are preserved.

Existing anonymous public catalog reads, account and billing unavailable truth, fixed 6.75 comparison FX, diagnostics, disabled configuration writes, inactive telemetry and updater boundaries remain intact, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, production or public-release resource is changed.

requirements.statement: Repair native macOS titlebar consistency and automatically resolve standalone-versus-bundled CLI coexistence without asking beginners to choose paths.
acceptance: Transparent native titlebar and fixed light/dark background retain native decorations. Do not force application or OS appearance, so system mode stays automatic.

Version 2 deduplicates canonical aliases, excludes macOS .app internal executables before probing, selects only standalone candidate or unique earliest absolute PATH candidate. Ties and common-only ambiguity remain unresolved with desktop/retry actions. No user installation or configuration changes.

Fixed five-tool closed projection includes independent and bundled counts and selection reason. Only selected candidate probed; never fall back silently after failure. Reject stale/malformed responses. v1 stays unchanged.

Plain four-locale copy distinguishes Codex CLI. Test native selection, React/IPC theme ordering and scan transitions, workbench/cost regression and exact signed notarized local Intel package. No account, DSH, server, updater or public release activation.

requirements.statement: RU-023 delivers an internal desktop 0.2.0 client integration with the fixed first-party NewAPI desktop v2 contract for browser authorization, secure remembered session, truthful account and cumulative usage, account-aware model pricing and first-party wallet opening without changing any server or tool configuration.
acceptance: Only https://yeschoy.com and https://api.yeschoy.com may be selected as API origins; redirects, caller-provided URLs, unrecognized bootstrap paths and a client version below the advertised minimum fail closed.

The system browser opens only the verified first-party authorization URL; the UI shows the non-secret short user code and explicit waiting, rejected, expired, cancelled, network and retry states without exposing the device code or any token.

Refresh token and session ID are stored only in macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager, the access token remains in native memory, and authenticated network calls occur only in the Rust layer with no secret returned to JavaScript, log, ordinary file, configuration, telemetry or diagnostic output.

A successful session shows the current username or display name, remaining balance, cumulative consumption, cumulative token usage, request count, server observation time and a retry action; absent or malformed fields remain unavailable instead of becoming zero.

The model page uses the current account's available model IDs and NewAPI pricing metadata, keeps exact model IDs visible, labels the fixed 6.75 conversion, and displays official-reference versus current-account rates only for ratio-priced rows whose inputs are complete; unsupported pricing is marked unavailable.

Recharge opens only the bootstrap-provided HTTPS wallet URL on the yeschoy.com first-party origin; logout revokes the current desktop session when possible and clears local credentials without changing browser sessions, tool keys or configurations.
Tool-key creation, DSH or other tool writes, backups, server code, database, Nginx, deployment, telemetry upload, updater activation and public release are outside RU-023.
The candidate and handoff state explicitly retain a production blocker until the server branch is deployed and desktop-issued sessions are restricted server-side to approved desktop routes.

requirements.statement: RU-024 turns the deployed NewAPI integration into one coherent internal functional client candidate with shared first-party account state, server-owned comparison conversion, authenticated models, and native-only one-click setup for Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex.
acceptance: Changing between mainland optimized and global accelerated never deletes or invalidates a valid desktop credential; only confirmed expiry, revocation, logout or an authenticated 401/403 clears it.
The overview, sidebar, account, model and setup destinations consume one shared account projection and cannot simultaneously label the same current session signed in and signed out.
The account model list is the selection authority for setup and prices; stale public-preview blockers and guest-only copy no longer disable an authenticated user.

The positive usd_exchange_rate from the selected NewAPI status response is displayed and used for comparable official-reference and current-account CNY prices; an absent or malformed rate makes comparison unavailable instead of falling back to 6.75.

One-click setup supports exactly Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex in this unit, validates one selected account model and compiled first-party line, and reports a closed success or recovery reason.

The native command reuses or creates one dedicated unrestricted NewAPI tool token for the selected target, prefixes it for relay use, never returns it to JavaScript, and deletes a newly created token if the local write cannot commit.

Claude setup changes only the owned env fields in the existing settings object; Codex setup changes only its active model/provider table and OPENAI_API_KEY. Existing unrelated fields are preserved, writes are atomic, and an in-memory transaction snapshot restores all touched files after failure without retained backup history.
DSH, OpenCode, Pi, other tool writes, NewAPI source, database schema, Nginx, DNS, deployment, telemetry, updater and public release remain outside RU-024.

requirements.statement: Make first setup and daily reuse simple without silent cost changes, secret exposure, lock-in or false success.
acceptance: Read-only full current-tree baseline proof before product edits; immutable historical failures/proofs.
Installed/connected apps first and missing apps expandable. Full model IDs, group ratios, comparison assumptions and restoration remain visible or accessible.

Native Open for Claude Desktop/Codex Desktop/DSH needs no account login, rewrites no settings, issues no tokens and sends no paid test. DSH reuses live process and starts on explicit Open after assistant relaunch. Opened is not a new provider-verification claim.
No arbitrary renderer paths/URLs/commands/credentials. Serialize open/restore/activation; preserve unrelated edits, reject pending recovery or changed owned provider identity.
Missing saved model/group never silently picks a replacement, even after refresh errors; explicit selection shows new price before apply.
Failure states expose relevant account, model, group, line, installation or recovery actions. Quit names affected applications and explains DSH reopening.

Native isolated regression, ordinary-account/empty-app/price-change/error/double-click renderer tests, type/build and light/dark/narrow keyboard checks. No Windows real-device or release claims without evidence.

requirements.statement: Display website-aligned account currency and auditable recent estimated savings without new backend privileges or invented historical totals.
acceptance: Current CNY status projects customer-facing RMB credits using quota_per_unit and usd_exchange_rate; missing/unsupported settings show unavailable, never USD or zero fallback. Cumulative consumed credits use account used_quota, not recent TPM.

Fetch only newest bounded 100 consumption records through the existing native desktop bearer and fixed first-party origin. Do not pass raw rows, metadata, credentials or user IDs into renderer IPC; failed logs do not sign out the account.

Match the website's quota, recorded special/group ratio, price and usd_exchange_rate formula for supported comparable records. Exclude malformed, non-consumption, free, subscription, special-fee and unknown basis records; both totals use the same included rows.

Keep negative savings truthful and distinguish available zero, no history, no comparable records, unavailable and refresh-stale states. Never imply recent-100-row calculations are cumulative/monthly or real cash savings.

Use a closed schema5 financial projection with finite bounded decimal strings, explicit counts and optional zero date window. Decoder preserves existing schema3/4 and rejects extra fields, impossible aggregates or signed-out finance.

Overview and account share currency/savings logic, provide concise receipt-like detail and current-rate explanation; retain actual usage as a secondary metric and clarify mainland/global network lines do not change price groups.

Run isolated native and renderer regressions, type/build, arithmetic and boundary fixtures plus local light/dark/narrow keyboard visual checks. No server changes or release/real-account validation claims.

requirements.statement: Implement explicitly selected model sets with real identity and fixed per-model billing routes, honest request errors and cooperative bounded exit without packaging or server mutation.
acceptance: Up to the documented 200-entry catalog bound, unique full model IDs bind explicit billing groups; default is a member. No silent cross-group fallback or enrollment of unselected models. Legacy records upgrade on explicit activation only.

All seven adapters publish native model menus/catalogs via authenticated loopback routing; legitimate native default changes are not configuration corruption. In-flight requests retain their route. Unsupported optional vendor menus do not block default use.
Credential sets remain inside OS credential storage, handle the Windows per-blob bound transactionally, and never expose full keys through renderer, files, errors or diagnostics.

Claude identity uses real IDs rather than Sonnet display masking; both bridges route requested model exactly and isolate continuation history. Curated HTTP/SSE errors and in-memory last-request observations never turn failed streams into success.

Window close offers background/cancel/exit globally. Confirmed exit rejects new operations, cancels safe work, preserves in-flight account mutations and local rollback, and stops owned runtimes with bounded grace and recoverable progress.

Synthetic transaction/route/stream/exit tests, actual renderer tests/typecheck/build and Windows compilation pass. No installer, signed release, server change or live-account success is inferred from these tests.

requirements.statement: Enable a remotely controllable domestic mirror for exact official Codex and Claude Desktop packages without weakening client-native trust checks or blocking publication on a separate legal-evidence file.
acceptance: The operator publisher needs no vendor-permission or source-approval JSON. It accepts only an exact current private candidate fetched from one of six compiled official origins, rechecks source metadata, package structure, identity, architecture, publisher, size and SHA256, and never grants the periodic synchronizer public-root write access.

Catalog schema 2 distinguishes native_verified from client_native_required. A valid matching native receipt is the only way to emit native_verified; absent receipt emits client_native_required and never claims server-side signature verification. The public catalog contains no approval, legal-basis, operator identity, credential or private-path fields.

The client accepts only the fixed ergou.qzz.io catalog and immutable source-slot/hash URL. Both verification states still pass through the same local macOS codesign, Team ID, bundle identity and Gatekeeper checks or Windows manifest, App Installer and installed-package trust checks before completion. A catalog assertion alone is never executable trust.

An operator can atomically disable every mirrored installer by publishing a valid empty catalog and false health projection without deleting objects or requiring a client update. Re-publication re-enables individual current candidates, prevents downgrade, preserves unrelated slots and previous immutable objects, and recovers safely after catalog or health interruption.

Missing, empty, stale, malformed, unsupported, corrupt, unavailable or disabled mirror state falls back to the compiled official path with truthful source UI and no account credentials. Mirror download failure never reuses partial bytes across source, URL, version, size or digest.

requirements.statement: Make one-click activation fast and uniform for all seven supported agents by separating atomic local configuration from asynchronous real-model observation and by safely handling applications that must reload settings.
acceptance: All seven targets share one completion rule: exact account model/group eligibility, native secure credential storage, atomic owned-field commit and semantic readback, required helper-owned loopback readiness, and applicable open dispatch. The activation button never sends or waits for a paid upstream model prompt.

If Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop is already running, the first request returns application_running without account, key or file mutation. After an explicit save-work confirmation, native code requests normal quit, never force termination, stops if the app remains open, and reopens the exact discovered installation after success.

Claude Code, Pi, Hermes and OpenClaw never terminate an existing terminal or editor session and plainly state that a new session uses the new settings. DSH may reuse or restart only its assistant-owned runtime.

A successfully read-back configuration remains connected when the first real model request later reports upstream timeout, quota, model or provider failure; that observation appears in the existing recent-connection result and can guide model or line switching.

Synthetic native and renderer tests cover every adapter, running/not-running/refused desktop lifecycle branches, no-force-kill behavior, rollback/reopen behavior, truthful copy, and macOS Apple-Silicon plus Windows compilation without packaging.

requirements.statement: Complete a signed, recoverable Yeschoy desktop self-update path for supported macOS and Windows builds while keeping update checks, downloads, installation and publication independent from application connection, third-party application installation and account/model traffic.
acceptance: The bundled app checks one compiled HTTPS stable channel in the background without blocking startup or connection work, reports no-update and unavailable states truthfully, and exposes update availability globally plus in Settings without forcing a modal.

One explicit user action downloads a mandatory-signature-verified artifact, presents bounded progress, cooperatively drains unrelated native operations and runtimes, installs, and relaunches where required; a failed install never leaves the UI pretending an update completed and attempts to relaunch the current app after shutdown has begun.

The renderer receives only closed update status, version, notes and byte counts through dedicated IPC; it receives no signing key, artifact path, raw endpoint error or direct updater-plugin authority. Update serialization is independent of tool activation, application installation, account, model and vendor-download state.

The release configuration embeds only the updater public key, creates updater artifacts for candidate builds, keeps the private key outside the repository and public origin, and replaces the inherited CC Switch release identity with Yeschoy-specific manual publication inputs.

The download origin serves an atomically published stable manifest when present and empty HTTP 204 when absent. Immutable versioned artifacts are published before the manifest, rollback disables the manifest without deleting old objects, and health truthfully reflects channel publication.

Happy, failure, replay, stale-version, race and recovery scenarios pass together with renderer, native and publisher tests. A first updater-aware build is identified as the one-time manual bootstrap boundary rather than claiming older clients can discover an updater they do not contain.

requirements.statement: Close the audited repository-owned public-release defects across all seven supported application integrations while preserving truthful release gates for external signing, notarization and stable-channel publication.
acceptance: Every authenticated local AI gateway accepts the established large-request limit only after authorization and under a shared nonblocking admission guard; oversized or concurrent pressure fails with a bounded closed response rather than multiplying full request buffers.

Dedicated application credentials are restricted to the exact selected model set and billing group, are reused only when that scope still matches, never cross renderer IPC, and are revoked or explicitly reported during a restore-and-logout flow.

Activation remains transactional across all seven adapters, reports bounded stage progress, supports cooperative cancellation at safe transaction boundaries, handles already-running desktop clients through the existing consented normal-quit path, and never leaves the workbench indefinitely blocked.

Child-process output and startup parsing are bounded, Windows launch helpers use qualified system paths, installed application identity is verified beyond a filename where the platform exposes identity, and exit behavior is reachable without Task Manager.
Installation, discovery and localization copy describe only behavior actually implemented for each target; unsupported one-click installation or incomplete languages are not advertised as complete.

Yeschoy release and update automation contains no inherited CC Switch bucket, repository or public-origin identity, verifies signed updater artifacts before manifest promotion, and fails closed when platform signing, notarization or publication credentials are absent.

Focused governed scenarios, frontend tests, TypeScript, production build, native tests, format, lints, dependency audits and source-level release checks pass. No package, upload, deployment, version bump or real user-state mutation occurs in this unit; unavailable external credentials remain explicit blockers.

A synchronous ready result requires the target credential in native secure storage, atomic configuration commit with semantic readback, the required helper-owned loopback runtime listening, and an applicable desktop or DSH open dispatch. It never waits for or bills an upstream model request.

Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop are checked again under the activation lock. If running and restartRunningApp is absent, application_running returns before mutation. With explicit consent native code requests a normal quit, waits only for a bounded exit, never force-terminates, and reopens only the exact discovered target.

A refused or incomplete normal quit leaves settings untouched and returns application_running with graceful_restart_required. CLI tools never terminate an existing terminal or editor session; their new configuration applies to a new session. Only helper-owned runtimes may be restarted.

Configuration, secure-storage, local-runtime and launch failures remain distinct closed outcomes. A failing local transaction restores touched files and prior credentials and deletes only a newly created token whose ownership is proven; a desktop app normally closed for the attempt is reopened against restored settings.

After ready, the first real application request is observed by the existing local gateway and exposed through recent connection results. An upstream timeout, quota, model or provider error does not roll back a configuration that was already atomically installed.
Complete keys never cross renderer IPC, appear in ordinary configuration or enter diagnostic text. Loopback compatibility endpoints return only public model metadata and health state.
Duplicate or unregistered model/group is rejected; no implicit default/group substitution. Cancellation before local write is safe; after write must restore locally or retain recovery state.

An installer handoff atomically consumes its one-use intent before credential or configuration work, checks full selection and exact installed target, and uses the captured native epoch throughout existing session-guarded activation.

A same-tool pending recovery record is self-healed only on a new explicit activation under the cross-process lock; incomplete file, credential or receipt cleanup remains non-ready with manual restore fallback.

Claude Desktop aliases are accepted only when derived from the current credential model set and resolve to exactly one real model, group and key before dispatch; Claude Code behavesAs never replaces the transmitted model ID.

error.freshness: The failed request cannot become current.
